extracted.subtask_description: Statutory and procedural standards from the U.S. patent statutes (as reproduced in the MPEP) governing patent term extension, statutory invention registrations, plant and design patents, secrecy orders, foreign filing, compensation, and related definitions and limits. Useful for evaluating eligibility, required content, and consequences under these statutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim extension application contents
rubrics_metrics.description: The application shall contain— (i) the identity of the product subject to regulatory review and the Federal statute under which such review is occurring; (ii) the identity of the patent for which interim extension is being sought and the identity of each claim of such patent which claims the product under regulatory review or a method of using or manufacturing the product; (iii) information to enable the Director to determine under subsection (a)(1), (2), and (3) the eligibility of a patent for extension; (iv) a brief description of the activities undertaken by the applicant during the applicable regulatory review period to date with respect to the product under review and the significant dates applicable to such activities; and (v) such patent or other information as the Director may require.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These five enumerated items are the mandatory contents for an interim-extension application; they form the factual and documentary basis the Director may rely on to determine eligibility under the statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director action on interim extension and certificate issuance
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Director determines that, except for permission to market or use the product commercially, the patent would be eligible for an extension of the patent term, the Director shall publish in the Federal Register a notice of such determination, including the identity of the product under regulatory review, and shall issue to the applicant a certificate of interim extension for a period of not more than 1 year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interim extension certificates are limited to 1 year; the Director publishes a notice and issues the certificate when preliminary eligibility (aside from marketing permission) is found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on number and timing of subsequent interim extension applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The owner of record of a patent, or its agent, for which an interim extension has been granted may apply for not more than 4 subsequent interim extensions under this paragraph, except that, in the case of a patent subject to subsection (g)(6)(C), the owner of record of the patent, or its agent, may apply for only 1 subsequent interim extension under this paragraph. Each such subsequent application shall be made during the period beginning 60 days before, and ending 30 days before, the expiration of the preceding interim extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies numerical caps on repeat interim-extension requests and the filing window for subsequent interim extension applications (60–30 days before expiration of the prior interim extension).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording and effect of interim extension certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: Each certificate of interim extension under this paragraph shall be recorded in the official file of the patent and shall be considered part of the original patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An interim extension certificate becomes part of the patent record and confers the recorded extension status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination and conversion rules for interim extensions upon marketing permission
rubrics_metrics.description: Any interim extension granted under this paragraph shall terminate at the end of the 60-day period beginning on the date on which the product involved receives permission for commercial marketing or use, except that, if within that 60-day period, the applicant notifies the Director of such permission and submits any additional information under paragraph (1) not previously contained in the application for interim extension, the patent shall be further extended— (i) for not to exceed 5 years from the date of expiration of the original patent term; or (ii) if the patent is subject to subsection (g)(6)(C), from the date on which the product involved receives approval for commercial marketing or use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interim extensions normally end 60 days after marketing permission; timely notification and submission of required information can trigger conversion to a full extension under the statutory limits (generally not to exceed 5 years total).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of rights during interim extension
rubrics_metrics.description: The rights derived from any patent the term of which is extended under this paragraph shall, during the period of interim extension— (i) in the case of a patent which claims a product, be limited to any use then under regulatory review; (ii) in the case of a patent which claims a method of using a product, be limited to any use claimed by the patent then under regulatory review; and (iii) in the case of a patent which claims a method of manufacturing a product, be limited to the method of manufacturing as used to make the product then under regulatory review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interim-extension rights are strictly limited to the subject matter and uses that are under regulatory review—they do not broadly expand patent scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director may base determination on applicant representations
rubrics_metrics.description: A determination that a patent is eligible for extension may be made by the Director solely on the basis of the representations contained in the application for the extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statute allows the Director to rely on applicant-submitted representations; however, issuance of a certificate requires that eligibility under subsection (a) and compliance with subsection (d) paragraphs (1)–(4) be satisfied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim extension pending final determination (temporary extensions)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the term of a patent for which an application has been submitted under subsection (d)(1) would expire before a certificate of extension is issued or denied, the Director shall extend, until such determination is made, the term of the patent for periods of up to one year if he determines that the patent is eligible for extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may grant one-year continuations of the patent term to prevent expiration while the extension application is pending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'product'
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of this section, the term 'product' means: (A) A drug product. (B) Any medical device, food additive, or color additive subject to regulation under the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statutory definition narrows which subject matter qualifies for regulatory-review-based term extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'drug product'
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'drug product' means the active ingredient of— (A) a new drug, antibiotic drug, or human biological product (as those terms are used in the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act and the Public Health Service Act), or (B) a new animal drug or veterinary biological product (as those terms are used in the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act and the Virus-Serum-Toxin Act) which is not primarily manufactured using recombinant DNA, recombinant RNA, hybridoma technology, or other processes involving site specific genetic manipulation techniques — including any salt or ester of the active ingredient, as a single entity or in combination with another active ingredient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines active-ingredient-based scope; excludes products primarily made by certain genetic-manipulation processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'major health or environmental effects test'
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'major health or environmental effects test' means a test which is reasonably related to the evaluation of the health or environmental effects of a product, which requires at least six months to conduct, and the data from which is submitted to receive permission for commercial marketing or use. Periods of analysis or evaluation of test results are not to be included in determining if the conduct of a test required at least six months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to determine regulatory-review-period start dates for food/color additives and animal products; clock measures active conduct time only (not analysis time).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions referencing statutory sections and terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Any reference to section 351 is to the Public Health Service Act; references to sections 503, 505, 512, or 515 refer to those sections of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act; reference to the Virus-Serum-Toxin Act is to the Act of March 4, 1913; 'informal hearing' has meaning in section 201(y) of the FD&C Act; 'patent' means a patent issued by the USPTO; 'date of enactment' is defined differently for human vs. animal products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies statutory cross-references and the meaning of key terms used elsewhere in the section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory review period: new drugs/human biologicals
rubrics_metrics.description: For a new drug, antibiotic drug, or human biological product, the regulatory review period is the sum of (i) the period beginning on the date an exemption under subsection (i) of section 505 or subsection (d) of section 507 became effective for the approved product and ending on the date an application was initially submitted for such drug product under section 351, 505, or 507, and (ii) the period beginning on the date the application was initially submitted for the approved product under section 351, subsection (b) of section 505, or section 507 and ending on the date such application was approved under such section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory-review period for human drugs is composed of a pre-submission exemption window plus the submission-to-approval interval; limitations in paragraph (6) apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory review period: food additives and color additives
rubrics_metrics.description: For a food additive or color additive, the regulatory review period is the sum of (i) the period beginning on the date a major health or environmental effects test on the additive was initiated and ending on the date a petition was initially submitted with respect to the product under the FD&C Act requesting issuance of a regulation for use of the product, and (ii) the period beginning on the date a petition was initially submitted and ending on the date such regulation became effective or, if objections were filed, when such objections were resolved and commercial marketing was permitted (with further provisions if marketing was later revoked and proceedings finally resolved).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captures both testing and petition/regulatory phases for additives; includes special resolution paths if objections delay effective regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory review period: medical devices
rubrics_metrics.description: For a medical device, the regulatory review period is the sum of (i) the period beginning on the date a clinical investigation on humans involving the device was begun and ending on the date an application was initially submitted with respect to the device under section 515, and (ii) the period beginning on the date an application was initially submitted under section 515 and ending on the date such application was approved under such Act or the period beginning on the date a notice of completion of a product development protocol was initially submitted under section 515(f)(5) and ending on the date the protocol was declared completed under section 515(f)(6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes either clinical-investigation-to-submission plus submission-to-approval, or the product-development-protocol pathway as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory review period: new animal drugs and veterinary biological products
rubrics_metrics.description: For new animal drugs, the regulatory review period is the sum of (i) the period beginning on the earlier of the date a major health or environmental effects test was initiated or the date an exemption under subsection (j) of section 512 became effective and ending on the date an application was initially submitted under section 512, and (ii) the period beginning on the date the application was initially submitted under subsection (b) of section 512 and ending on the date such application was approved. For veterinary biological products, the regulatory period is the sum of the period from authority to prepare an experimental biological product to license application submission, and from license submission to license issuance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Animal-product regulatory periods mirror the human-product structure: testing/exemption phase plus application-to-approval/license phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on periods determined (caps on extension)
rubrics_metrics.description: A period determined under any of the preceding paragraphs is subject to the following limitations: (A) If the patent involved was issued after the date of enactment of this section, the period of extension determined on the basis of the regulatory review period may not exceed five years. (B) If the patent involved was issued before the date of the enactment of this section and — (text sets out special caps and rules, including differing caps (e.g., two years, three years) in specified circumstances).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statute imposes absolute caps (generally five years) on extension based on regulatory-review periods; special transitional caps apply to patents issued before enactment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director authority to establish fees
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may establish such fees as the Director determines appropriate to cover the costs to the Office of receiving and acting upon applications under this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows the USPTO to charge fees related to term-extension processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Covered-date rule for controlled-substance recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Secretary of Health and Human Services provides notice to the sponsor of an application or request for approval, conditional approval, or indexing of a drug product for which the Secretary intends to recommend controls under the Controlled Substances Act, beginning on the covered date, the drug product shall be considered to (A) have been approved or indexed under the relevant provision and (B) have permission for commercial marketing or use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates a statutory fiction treating certain controlled-substance-regulated products as approved/indexed for purposes of term-extension timing; 'covered date' is separately defined by enumerated events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'covered date'
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'covered date' means the later of: (A) the date an application is approved under specified PHS/FD&C Act provisions; (B) the date an application is conditionally approved under section 571(b); (C) the date a request for indexing is granted under section 572(d); or (D) the date of issuance of the interim final rule controlling the drug under section 201(j) of the Controlled Substances Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates the triggering events that fix the covered date for controlled-substance-affected products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory invention registration eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director is authorized to publish a statutory invention registration containing the specification and drawings of a regularly filed application for a patent without examination if the applicant— (1) meets the requirements of section 112; (2) has complied with the requirements for printing, as set forth in regulations of the Director; (3) waives the right to receive a patent on the invention within such period as may be prescribed by the Director; and (4) pays application, publication, and other processing fees established by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication as a statutory invention registration is an alternative to patent prosecution if the applicant satisfies the listed conditions; interference rules may prevent publication until priority is determined in applicant's favor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect and attributes of statutory invention registration
rubrics_metrics.description: A statutory invention registration published pursuant to this section shall have all of the attributes specified for patents in this title except those specified in section 183 and sections 271 through 289; it shall not have any of the attributes specified for patents in any other provision of law. The invention with respect to which a statutory invention certificate is published is not a patented invention for purposes of section 292.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies which patent attributes apply to a statutory invention registration and clarifies its legal effect (not equivalent to a patent for certain statutes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Director reporting on statutory invention registrations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall report to Congress annually on the use of statutory invention registrations. Such report shall include assessment of federal agencies' use, how it aids management of federally developed technology, and cost savings to the Federal Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates oversight/assessment of the statutory registration program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plant-patent eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Whoever invents or discovers and asexually reproduces any distinct and new variety of plant, including cultivated sports, mutants, hybrids, and newly found seedlings, other than a tuber propagated plant or a plant found in an uncultivated state, may obtain a patent therefor, subject to the conditions and requirements of this title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plant patents are limited to asexually reproduced, distinct, new varieties and exclude certain classes (tuber-propagated, uncultivated plants). Other patent-title provisions apply except as provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plant-patent description and claim requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: No plant patent shall be declared invalid for noncompliance with section 112 if the description is as complete as is reasonably possible. The claim in the specification shall be in formal terms to the plant shown and described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relaxed strictness compared to general sec.112 requirements: completeness 'as reasonably possible' suffices; claims must formally refer to the plant as shown and described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plant-patent grant scope
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of a plant patent, the grant shall include the right to exclude others from asexually reproducing the plant, and from using, offering for sale, or selling the plant so reproduced, or any of its parts, throughout the United States, or from importing the plant so reproduced, or any parts thereof, into the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the exclusive rights conferred by a plant patent (as to asexual reproduction, commercialization, and importation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assistance of the Department of Agriculture for plant patents
rubrics_metrics.description: The President may by Executive order direct the Secretary of Agriculture, in accordance with the requests of the Director, to (1) furnish available information of the Department of Agriculture, (2) to conduct research upon special problems, or (3) to detail officers and employees of the Department to the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enables USDA support for patent-related plant issues at the Director's request via Executive order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design-patent eligibility and filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: Whoever invents any new, original, and ornamental design for an article of manufacture may obtain a patent therefor, subject to the conditions and requirements of this title. The filing date of an application for patent for design shall be the date on which the specification as prescribed by section 112 and any required drawings are filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design patents require novelty, originality, and ornamentality; proper specification and drawings determine the filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design right of priority
rubrics_metrics.description: The right of priority provided for by subsections (a) through (d) of section 119 shall be six months in the case of designs. The right of priority provided for by section 119(e) shall not apply to designs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design applications get a six-month foreign-priority window under the cited subsections; certain priority rules (119(e)) do not apply to designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Term of design patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents for designs shall be granted for the term of 15 years from the date of grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-2015 design patents have a 15-year term measured from grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secrecy orders for national security (withholding publication/grant)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever publication or disclosure by the publication of an application or by the grant of a patent on an invention in which the Government has a property interest might, in the opinion of the head of the interested Government agency, be detrimental to the national security, the Commissioner upon being so notified shall order that the invention be kept secret and shall withhold the publication of an application or the grant of a patent. The Commissioner shall also make the application available for inspection to designated defense and agency officials, and those individuals shall sign dated acknowledgments entered in the file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secrecy orders are initiated upon agency determination of detriment to national security; disclosure is tightly controlled and documented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration, renewal, and rescission of secrecy orders
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention shall not be ordered kept secret for a period of more than one year; the Commissioner shall renew the order at the end of any period upon notification by the head of the issuing department that national interest continues to require secrecy. Orders issued during war remain in effect for the duration of hostilities and one year after; orders during a declared national emergency remain in effect for the duration and six months thereafter. The Commissioner may rescind any order upon notification that disclosure is no longer detrimental to national security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies renewal mechanics, wartime and emergency extensions, and rescission pathway.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment for unauthorized disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: The invention disclosed in an application subject to a secrecy order may be held abandoned if it is established that the invention has been published or disclosed in violation of the order or that an application for a patent has been filed in a foreign country by the inventor (or those in privity) without consent of the Commissioner. The abandonment is held to have occurred as of the time of violation, and the consent to foreign filing shall not be given without concurrence of the heads of the departments and agencies which caused the order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unauthorized publication or foreign filing in violation of a secrecy order can cause abandonment and forfeiture of claims against the United States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to compensation for secrecy orders and government use
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant whose patent is withheld shall have the right, beginning at the date the applicant is notified that, except for the order, the application is otherwise in condition for allowance (or Feb 1, 1952, whichever is later) and ending six years after a patent is issued, to apply to the head of any department or agency who caused the order to be issued for compensation for the damage caused by the order of secrecy and/or for the use of the invention by the Government. The head of the department or agency may enter into agreement or award a sum not exceeding 75% of the sum considered just compensation if full settlement cannot be effected. A claimant may sue in the Court of Federal Claims or appropriate District Court to obtain the remainder. The right to compensation for use begins on the date of first use by the Government. The United States may avail itself of defenses under section 1498. No right of action is conferred on persons who invented the invention while in full-time employment or service of the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets the procedural window, remedies, settlement cap, and litigation venues for compensation claims arising from secrecy orders and government use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign filing restrictions and license requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Except when authorized by a license obtained from the Commissioner, a person shall not file in any foreign country prior to six months after filing in the United States an application for patent or for registration of a utility model, industrial design, or model in respect of an invention made in this country. A license shall not be granted with respect to an invention subject to a secrecy order without concurrence of the heads of the departments and agencies who caused the order. A license may be granted retroactively where an application has been filed abroad through error and the application does not disclose an invention within the scope of section 181.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires a pre-filing waiting period for foreign filings (six months) absent a license; strict controls apply where secrecy orders are involved; retroactive licenses limited to error cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of license and treatment of subsequent modifications
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'application' includes modifications, amendments, supplements, or divisions. The scope of a license shall permit subsequent modifications, amendments, and supplements containing additional subject matter if the U.S. application upon which the request for the license is based was not required to be made available for inspection under section 181 and if such changes do not change the general nature of the invention in a manner which would require inspection under section 181. If a license was not required, such subsequent modifications, amendments, and supplements may be made, without a license, to the application filed in the foreign country if the U.S. application was not required to be made available under section 181 and such changes do not change the general nature of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines how licenses interact with subsequent changes to applications and when foreign amendments are permitted without a license.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent barred for foreign filing without license (sanction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person shall not receive a United States patent for an invention if that person, without procuring the license prescribed in section 184, has filed in a foreign country prior to six months after filing in the United States an application for a patent or registration. A U.S. patent issued to such person shall be invalid, unless the failure to procure such license was through error and the patent does not disclose subject matter within the scope of section 181.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a strong sanction (invalidity) for premature foreign filings absent an obtained license, subject to a narrow error exception.
